newsitem.title: FRANCE: Juppe's popularity in France matches record low.
newsitem.headline: Juppe's popularity in France matches record low.

text.p: French Prime Minister Alain Juppe's popularity has sunk to match an all-time low while President Jacques Chirac's standing has risen, an opinion poll published on Wednesday showed.
Pollster CSA said it was the first time the two leaders' ratings had moved apart since Chirac and Juppe came to office in 1995.

The divergence was likely to draw attention once again to the problem Juppe's deep unpopularity could pose as he leads the centre-right coalition's campaign for a snap National Assembly election on May 25 and June 1.
Other opinion polls show the government retaining a sharply reduced majority.

The poll, for La Vie magazine and France Info radio, showed Juppe had a favourable rating from just 28 percent of those surveyed, matching his all-time low last year. In March, Juppe's approval rating stood at 30 percent and in February 32 percent.
Sixty-five percent had an unfavourable opinion of the prime minister, compared to 61 percent a month ago.

Chirac's ratings rose with 41 percent expressing support compared to 36 percent in March. Fifty-three percent rated him unfavourably compared to 55 percent in March. The CSA pollsters questioned 910 people on April 24 and 25.
A separate Sofres poll for Le Figaro Magazine also found that Juppe's ratings had uncoupled from Chirac's for the first time.

Just 28 percent of those surveyed said they wanted Juppe to play a major role in months and years to come, against 32 percent a month ago. Chirac's rating was stable, with 38 percent wanting him to play a major role.

Opposition Socialist leader Lionel Jospin's rating climbed four points to 51 percent, a higher rating than any leader on the centre-right and just behind former Socialist European Commission president Jacques Delors on 55 percent.
The survey questioned 1,000 people from April 23 to 25.
